chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him):

It has been reported from the two Truthful Ones (peace be upon them) that: 'Circumcise your children on the seventh day to purify them, and indeed the earth resounds with noise to Allah from the urine of the uncircumcised.' And I, may I be your ransom, said: The surgeons of our city are not skilled in that, and they do not circumcise him on the seventh day. And among us is a Jewish surgeon, so is it permissible for the Jew to circumcise the children of the Muslims or not, if Allah wills?
So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The Sunnah is on the seventh day, therefore do not oppose the Sunnah, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: When should a Muslim boy be circumcised according to Shia hadith, and is it permissible for a Jew to perform the procedure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the seventh day as the normative time for male circumcision, linking it to ritual purity and the concept of the earth 'groaning' from the urine of the uncircumcised. It further clarifies the permissibility of non-Muslims, specifically Jews, performing the procedure for Muslims, affirming that the specific practitioner does not invalidate the established Sunnah of the seventh day.
